headline: Record quarter, margin dip on pay costs, guidance raised
summary_short: Cummins posted record Q2 2026 revenue of $9.46 billion (+9% y/y) and net income of $932 million ($6.73 diluted EPS), while EBITDA margin slipped 90bps to 17.5% on higher incentive compensation. The company raised full-year revenue growth guidance to +10%-13% and EBITDA margin guidance to 18.0%-18.5%.
summary_long: Record Q2 revenue of $9.46B (+9% y/y) was led by Power Systems (+19%) and Distribution (+9%), both driven by data-center power-generation demand; Engine (+6%) and Components (+7%) grew on North American and Chinese truck demand. Net income was $932M (+4.7% y/y, $6.73 diluted EPS), including $29M of unfavorable discrete tax items. EBITDA of $1.65B (+4.2% y/y) fell to 17.5% of sales from 18.4%, driven by higher incentive compensation tied to expected record full-year results; management expects margin improvement in H2. Cummins raised FY2026 revenue guidance to +10%-13% (from +8%-11%) and EBITDA margin guidance to 18.0%-18.5% (from 17.75%-18.5%), raised the quarterly dividend to $2.20/share, and returned $501M to shareholders. Cash rose to $3.18B.

drivers.explanation: Demand for standby power for data centers and improving North American truck markets drove record results; management raised full-year guidance and expects the second half to be stronger than the first.

North America sales rose 8% and international revenue rose 12% (led by China); Power Systems and Distribution were driven by data-center power-generation demand, Engine and Components by stronger North American and Chinese truck markets.

Margin compression across the company and most segments was primarily due to higher incentive compensation tied to expected record full-year results; management expects EBITDA % to be higher in H2 and full-year 2026 versus 2025.
Growth was tempered by a 25.1% effective tax rate including $29 million ($0.21 per diluted share) of unfavorable discrete tax items.
